title: Sep 16 Results + Sep 17 Preview: When the Model Finds Its Groove
summary: 73.3% accuracy on Sep 16—11 wins, 4 losses. Tomorrow we're backing the Brewers again.

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Yesterday

Sometimes you can feel it when the model is locked in, and September 16th was one of those days. We went 11-4 across the slate, hitting 73.3% of our picks. That's the kind of performance that reminds you why we trust the numbers, even when the occasional miss humbles us.

## The Wins That Stood Out

The Guardians came through at 61% confidence against the White Sox—exactly the kind of solid favorite that delivers. The Orioles took care of business against the Mets at 59%, and the Cubs held serve against the Braves in a 61% pick that felt right from the start.

But here's what I love: even our tightest call of the day, the Giants at just 51% over the Cardinals, came through. Sometimes baseball rewards you for trusting the slimmest of edges.

content.title: Sep 16 Prediction Results by Confidence Level

content.value:
## The Two That Got Away

No perfect days here—we're not afraid to talk about the misses. The Yankees fell to the Twins despite our 54% confidence, and the Dodgers couldn't get past the Reds at 61%. Both were reasonable picks that just didn't pan out. That's baseball, and that's why we track everything.

## Looking Ahead to September 17

Now let's talk about tomorrow. The model is pointing us right back to a matchup we liked yesterday: the Milwaukee Brewers visiting the Pittsburgh Pirates.

Kyle Harrison gets the ball for Milwaukee, facing off against Wilber Dotel for Pittsburgh. Our confidence sits at 52%—this is closer than yesterday's 61% Brewers pick, but the model still sees value here.

content.sub: Pick: Brewers · 52% confidence · Harrison vs Dotel

content.value:
## Why the Brewers Again?

Here's the thing: when a team delivers at 61% one day, and the model still likes them the next—even at a lower confidence—that continuity matters. Milwaukee proved they can handle Pittsburgh's ballpark. The pitching matchup favors them just enough to warrant our attention.

Is 52% a slam dunk? No. But it's an edge, and over a full season, those edges are what separate the good models from the lucky guesses.
